copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Belgium v Egypt in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Monday, and the model and the market disagree on the Egypt side by +11.4pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Public Elo rates Belgium 100 points higher than the other side (Belgium 1860, Egypt 1760). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Belgium to win at 49%, the draw at 24%, and Egypt to win at 27%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Egypt sits at 27% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Belgium to win at 57%, the draw at 24%, and Egypt to win at 16%. Kalshi has Egypt at 16%, which prices out at American odds of +525; the model has the same side at 27%. The +11.4pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Egypt, that haircut lands the model at 22%; the market is at 16%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +6.4pp. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Egypt side.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 24 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Egypt a stronger prior than the Kalshi line implies.
The +11.4pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

editorial_citations.quote: Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah is named in Egypt's preliminary World Cup squad, which will be trimmed by one player this month.

copy.summary: A +11.4pp gap across model and market on the Egypt side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Egypt at 27%; Kalshi sits at 16%.
copy.title: Belgium v Egypt · the model leans Egypt
